1.1.title: Basic Concepts (Ohm's law, circuits, KCL/KVL, star-delta)

qa.q: What is the SI unit of resistivity?
qa.a: Ω·m (ohm-metre). From R = ρL/A, ρ = RA/L.

qa.q: If a wire is stretched to twice its length at constant volume, its resistance becomes
qa.a: 4 times. Length doubles and area halves, so R = ρ(2L)/(A/2) = 4R.

qa.q: Three 6 Ω resistors in series give
qa.a: 18 Ω. Series: Req = R₁ + R₂ + R₃.

qa.q: Ohm's law is not applicable to
qa.a: non-linear devices such as diodes, transistors and arc lamps.

qa.q: A 60 W and a 100 W bulb (both rated 220 V) are connected in series across 220 V. Which glows brighter?
qa.a: The 60 W bulb. It has higher resistance (R = V²/P), and the same current flows, so P = I²R is larger.

1.1.keyPoints: Two resistors in parallel: Req = R₁R₂/(R₁ + R₂). Current divider: I₁ = I × R₂/(R₁ + R₂).

1.2.title: Network Theorems, RLC Circuits and Power

qa.q: Thevenin resistance is found by
qa.a: killing all independent sources (V short, I open) and finding the resistance seen from the load terminals.

qa.q: The bandwidth of a series RLC circuit is
qa.a: BW = R/(2πL) Hz, with Q = f₀/BW.

qa.q: Power factor of a purely resistive circuit is
qa.a: 1 (unity), since φ = 0°.

qa.q: Impedance of a series RL circuit with R = 3 Ω and XL = 4 Ω is
Reciprocity theorem applies to
qa.a: linear bilateral networks with a single source.

1.2.keyPoints: Power triangle: S² = P² + Q². P = VI cos φ (W), Q = VI sin φ (VAR), S = VI (VA).

1.3.title: Alternating Current Fundamentals and Three-Phase Systems

qa.q: The instantaneous value of v = Vm sin(ωt) at ωt = 30° is
qa.a: 0.5 Vm, since sin 30° = 0.5.

qa.q: The RMS value of a half-wave rectified sine of peak Vm is
qa.a: Vm/2. Its average value is Vm/π.

qa.q: The RMS value of a full-wave rectified sine is
qa.a: Vm/√2, the same as a full sine wave. Its average is 2Vm/π.

qa.q: The number of wires in a three-phase four-wire system is
qa.a: 4 (three lines and one neutral).

qa.q: The speed of an alternator with P poles producing f Hz is
qa.a: Ns = 120f/P rpm. A 4-pole, 50 Hz machine runs at 1500 rpm.

1.3.keyPoints: Two-wattmeter method: total power P = W₁ + W₂. tan φ = √3(W₁ − W₂)/(W₁ + W₂).

1.4.title: Semiconductor Devices (Diode, BJT, MOSFET, CMOS)

qa.q: Diode current equation
qa.a: I = Is(e^(V/ηVT) − 1), with VT ≈ 26 mV at room temperature.

qa.q: The ripple factor of a full-wave rectifier (without filter) is
qa.a: about 0.482. For a half-wave rectifier it is 1.21.

qa.q: Efficiency of a full-wave rectifier (max) is
The PIV of a centre-tap full-wave rectifier diode is
qa.a: 2Vm. For a bridge rectifier it is Vm.

qa.q: In a BJT, the most heavily doped region is the
qa.a: emitter. The base is thin and lightly doped; the collector is the largest.

1.4.keyPoints: In a MOSFET in saturation: ID = k(VGS − VT)². The threshold voltage VT separates cut-off from conduction.

1.5.title: Signal Generators and Oscillators

qa.q: An oscillator uses
qa.a: positive feedback. Amplifiers use negative feedback for stability.

qa.q: The frequency of a 555 astable is
qa.a: f = 1.44/((RA + 2RB)C). Duty cycle = (RA + RB)/(RA + 2RB).

qa.q: Pulse width of a 555 monostable is
Series and parallel resonance frequencies of a crystal are
qa.a: very close; fs is slightly lower than fp.

qa.q: A Schmitt trigger is used to
qa.a: convert slowly varying or noisy signals into clean square waves (it has hysteresis).

1.5.keyPoints: Oscillator types: RC (phase-shift, Wien bridge) for audio; LC (Colpitts, Hartley, Clapp) for RF; crystal for high stability.

1.6.title: Amplifiers and Op-amps

qa.q: The gain-bandwidth product of an op-amp is
qa.a: constant: closed-loop gain × bandwidth = unity-gain bandwidth (≈1 MHz for 741).

qa.q: Output of an ideal op-amp integrator is
qa.a: Vo = −(1/RC)∫Vin dt.

qa.q: Output of an ideal op-amp differentiator is
qa.a: Vo = −RC dVin/dt.

qa.q: A summing amplifier with equal resistors gives
qa.a: Vo = −(V₁ + V₂ + V₃).

qa.q: The op-amp comparator operates in
qa.a: open loop; the output saturates at ±Vsat depending on which input is larger.

1.6.keyPoints: Efficiency ranking: Class A (25–50%) < Class AB < Class B (78.5%) < Class C (up to ~90%). Distortion ranking is the reverse.

2.1.title: Digital Logic (Number Systems, Gates, Boolean Algebra, K-map)

qa.q: The radix of the hexadecimal system is
qa.a: 16 (digits 0–9 and A–F).

qa.q: Binary 1101.101 in decimal is
Minimum NOR gates to realize an AND gate
qa.a: 3 (invert both inputs, then NOR them).

qa.q: The dual of A + 0 = A is
qa.a: A · 1 = A (swap + with · and 0 with 1).

qa.q: Don't-care conditions in a K-map are
qa.a: treated as 0 or 1, whichever gives the larger groups.

2.1.keyPoints: Number of minterms for n variables = 2^n. SOP uses minterms (Σm); POS uses maxterms (ΠM).

2.2.title: Combinational and Arithmetic Circuits

qa.q: A full adder has how many inputs and outputs?
qa.a: 3 inputs (A, B, Cin) and 2 outputs (Sum, Cout).

qa.q: The carry of a full adder is
qa.a: Cout = AB + BCin + ACin.

qa.q: A carry look-ahead adder is faster than a ripple-carry adder because
qa.a: it generates carries in parallel using generate (G = AB) and propagate (P = A⊕B) terms.

qa.q: The number of 4:1 MUXes needed to build a 16:1 MUX
qa.a: 5 (four in the first stage, one in the second).

qa.q: Magnitude comparator outputs
qa.a: A > B, A = B and A < B.

2.2.keyPoints: 2's complement of X = 1's complement + 1. Subtraction A − B = A + (2's complement of B).

2.3.title: Sequential Logic Circuits

qa.q: A counter that counts 0 to 9 and resets is
qa.a: a decade (BCD, mod-10) counter.

qa.q: The characteristic equation of a JK flip-flop is
qa.a: Q(t+1) = JQ' + K'Q.

qa.q: The characteristic equation of an SR flip-flop is
qa.a: Q(t+1) = S + R'Q, with SR = 0.

qa.q: Shift register that allows loading all bits at once and reading all at once
qa.a: PIPO (parallel-in parallel-out).

qa.q: Maximum clock frequency of an n-stage ripple counter
qa.a: f ≤ 1/(n × tpd), where tpd is one flip-flop's delay.

2.3.keyPoints: Latch = level-triggered; flip-flop = edge-triggered. Mod-N counter needs ⌈log₂N⌉ flip-flops.

2.4.title: Microprocessor Architecture and Assembly Language

qa.q: The 8085 has how many pins?
qa.a: 40 pins, operating from a single +5 V supply.

qa.q: The 8085 has how many general-purpose 8-bit registers?
qa.a: 6 (B, C, D, E, H, L), usable as pairs BC, DE, HL.

qa.q: The instruction DAA is used for
qa.a: decimal adjust after BCD addition.

qa.q: Number of T-states for an opcode fetch in 8085
qa.a: 4 T-states (4 or 6 depending on the instruction).

qa.q: Segment registers in 8086
qa.a: CS, DS, SS and ES.

2.4.keyPoints: 8085 instruction groups: data transfer, arithmetic, logical, branching, machine control.

2.5.title: Microprocessor System (Memory, PPI, Serial Interface, DMA)

qa.q: The 8253/8254 is a
qa.a: programmable interval timer/counter with three 16-bit counters.

qa.q: The 8237 is a
qa.a: DMA controller with 4 channels.

qa.q: Memory-mapped I/O means
qa.a: I/O devices share the memory address space and are accessed with memory instructions (e.g. MOV, LDA).

qa.q: Access time is lowest for
qa.a: SRAM among memory chips (used for cache).

qa.q: Number of address lines needed for 1 MB memory

2.5.keyPoints: DMA modes: burst (block), cycle stealing, transparent (hidden).

2.6.title: Interrupt Operations

qa.q: RST 5.5 vector address
RST 6.5 vector address
RST 7.5 is triggered by
qa.a: a rising edge; RST 6.5 and 5.5 are level-triggered.

qa.q: INT n instruction in 8086 is
qa.a: a software interrupt that jumps to the ISR whose address is in the IVT at n × 4.

qa.q: Which interrupt has the lowest priority in 8085?
qa.a: INTR.

2.6.keyPoints: Hardware interrupts come from external pins; software interrupts come from instructions (RST n in 8085, INT n in 8086).

3.1.title: Introduction to C Programming

qa.q: What is the output of printf("%d", 5 > 3 > 1);?
qa.a: 0. 5 > 3 gives 1, then 1 > 1 is false (0).

qa.q: Which storage class retains its value between function calls?
qa.a: static.

qa.q: What is the default value of an uninitialized global int in C?
qa.a: 0. Local (auto) variables contain garbage.

qa.q: Which header is needed for strlen, strcpy and strcmp?
qa.a: <string.h>.

qa.q: The value of 10 >> 1 is
qa.a: 5 (right shift by 1 divides by 2).

3.1.keyPoints: Operator precedence (high to low): () [] → unary (++ -- ! sizeof) → * / % → + - → shifts → relational → == != → & → ^ → | → && → || → ?: → assignment → comma.

3.2.title: Pointers, Structures and Data Files in C

qa.q: What is the size of a pointer on a 64-bit system?
qa.a: Usually 8 bytes, regardless of the type it points to.

qa.q: What does a void pointer mean?
qa.a: A generic pointer that can hold any address; it must be cast before being dereferenced.

qa.q: Function used to resize dynamically allocated memory
qa.a: realloc().

qa.q: Difference between "w" and "w+" modes
qa.a: "w" is write-only; "w+" allows both reading and writing (the file is truncated).

qa.q: What does fgets(str, n, fp) read?
qa.a: At most n−1 characters or up to a newline, storing '\0' at the end.

3.2.keyPoints: Structure vs union: structure size = sum of members (+ padding), all members usable together; union size = largest member, one member at a time.

3.3.title: C++ Constructs: Objects and Classes

qa.q: When is a copy constructor called?
qa.a: When an object is initialized from another object, passed by value, or returned by value.

qa.q: What is a default constructor?
qa.a: A constructor that takes no arguments (or has all default arguments).

qa.q: Can a constructor be private?
qa.a: Yes. It is used in the Singleton pattern to stop outside object creation.

qa.q: Which operator is used to allocate memory in C++?
qa.a: new (and delete to release it).

qa.q: What is an initializer list used for?
qa.a: Initializing const members, reference members and base classes in a constructor.

3.3.keyPoints: OOP pillars: encapsulation, abstraction, inheritance, polymorphism.

3.4.title: Features of Object-Oriented Programming

qa.q: Which operator is overloaded for cout << obj?
qa.a: operator<< as a friend (non-member) function taking ostream& and the object.

qa.q: Is the constructor of a base class inherited?
qa.a: No. Constructors are not inherited, but the base constructor is called when a derived object is created.

qa.q: Function overriding differs from overloading because
qa.a: overriding redefines a base-class function with the same signature in a derived class; overloading uses different signatures in the same scope.

qa.q: Multilevel inheritance example
qa.a: A → B → C, where C derives from B, which derives from A.

qa.q: Class-to-class conversion is done using
qa.a: a one-argument constructor in the destination class or a conversion operator in the source class.

3.4.keyPoints: Access after inheritance — public: pub→pub, prot→prot; protected: pub/prot→prot; private: pub/prot→private. Base private members are never directly accessible.

3.5.title: Virtual Functions and File Handling in C++

qa.q: Can we create a pointer to an abstract class?
qa.a: Yes. Pointers and references are allowed; only objects cannot be created.

qa.q: What is early binding?
qa.a: Resolving the function call at compile time (non-virtual functions, overloading).

qa.q: Which function returns the current get-pointer position in a file stream?
qa.a: tellg() (tellp() for the put pointer).

qa.q: Which function moves the get pointer in a file stream?
qa.a: seekg() (seekp() for the put pointer).

qa.q: What does endl do?
qa.a: Inserts a newline and flushes the output buffer.

3.5.keyPoints: Stream error states: goodbit, eofbit, failbit, badbit; check with good(), eof(), fail(), bad().

3.6.title: Generic Programming and Exception Handling

qa.q: Difference between vector and list
qa.a: vector is a dynamic array (fast random access); list is a doubly linked list (fast insertion/deletion anywhere).

qa.q: Which STL container follows LIFO?
qa.a: stack (a container adapter).

qa.q: Which STL container follows FIFO?
qa.a: queue (a container adapter).

qa.q: What is template specialization?
qa.a: Providing a separate implementation of a template for a specific type.

qa.q: Can a constructor throw an exception?
qa.a: Yes, and it is the standard way to signal construction failure (the destructor is not called for that object).

3.6.keyPoints: Exception flow: throw → stack unwinding (local objects destroyed) → first matching catch. Use noexcept for non-throwing functions.

4.1.title: Control and Central Processing Units

qa.q: The number of stages in a classic RISC pipeline
qa.a: 5: IF, ID, EX, MEM, WB.

qa.q: Horizontal vs vertical microprogramming
qa.a: Horizontal: wide words with one bit per control signal (fast, more memory). Vertical: encoded fields (compact, needs decoding).

qa.q: In register indirect addressing, the effective address is
qa.a: the content of the specified register.

qa.q: An instruction format with opcode 8 bits and address 16 bits has total length
qa.a: 24 bits.

qa.q: Superscalar processors
qa.a: issue more than one instruction per clock cycle using multiple pipelines.

4.1.keyPoints: CPI = cycles per instruction; CPU time = instruction count × CPI × clock period.

4.2.title: Computer Arithmetic and Memory System

qa.q: A cache has 2^k lines and memory has 2^m blocks in direct mapping. The tag bits are
qa.a: m − k.

qa.q: Set-associative cache: a 4-way cache with 64 lines has how many sets?
Number of bits in a memory address for 4 GB byte-addressable memory
Miss penalty is
qa.a: the extra time needed to fetch a block from the lower level on a cache miss.

qa.q: Main memory is usually implemented using
qa.a: DRAM; cache using SRAM.

4.2.keyPoints: Cache address split — Direct: Tag | Line | Word. Set-associative: Tag | Set | Word. Fully associative: Tag | Word.

4.3.title: Input-Output Organization and Multiprocessors

qa.q: Which data transfer mode is fastest for large blocks?
qa.a: DMA in burst mode.

qa.q: Interrupt-driven I/O is better than programmed I/O because
qa.a: the CPU can do other work until the device interrupts.

qa.q: An Omega network is a type of
qa.a: multistage interconnection network built from 2×2 switches.

qa.q: MESI protocol states
qa.a: Modified, Exclusive, Shared, Invalid.

qa.q: The I/O processor (IOP)
qa.a: is a dedicated processor that handles I/O operations, relieving the CPU.

4.3.keyPoints: Amdahl's law: speedup = 1/((1 − f) + f/p), where f = parallelizable fraction and p = number of processors.

4.4.title: Hardware-Software Design Issues in Embedded Systems

qa.q: Examples of embedded systems
qa.a: washing machine controllers, microwave ovens, digital cameras, routers, car ECUs, pacemakers.

qa.q: Design metrics of embedded systems
qa.a: NRE cost, unit cost, size, performance, power, flexibility, time-to-market, maintainability, correctness, safety.

qa.q: Difference between GPP and single-purpose processor
qa.a: GPP: flexible, programmable, low NRE. Single-purpose: fast, small, low power, high NRE, not programmable.

qa.q: An emulator vs simulator
qa.a: A simulator imitates the target in software on the host; an emulator uses hardware to mimic the target in the real circuit.

qa.q: The IC technologies for embedded systems include
qa.a: full-custom VLSI, semi-custom ASIC (gate array, standard cell), and PLDs/FPGAs.

4.4.keyPoints: Processor technology choices: general-purpose, application-specific (ASIP), single-purpose. IC technology choices: full-custom, semi-custom, PLD.

4.5.title: Real-Time Operating and Control Systems

qa.q: Task states in an RTOS
qa.a: ready, running, blocked (waiting), and suspended/dormant.

qa.q: Mutex vs semaphore
qa.a: A mutex has ownership and is used for mutual exclusion; a counting semaphore tracks available resources and can be signaled by any task.

qa.q: Schedulability bound for RMS with n tasks
qa.a: U ≤ n(2^(1/n) − 1), about 69% for large n.

qa.q: Schedulability condition for EDF
qa.a: total utilization U = Σ(Ci/Ti) ≤ 1.

qa.q: Components of a closed-loop control system
qa.a: reference input, controller, plant, sensor (feedback), and error detector.

4.5.keyPoints: Latency = time from event to start of response; jitter = variation in latency. An RTOS minimizes both.

4.6.title: Hardware Description Language (VHDL) and IC Technology

qa.q: VHDL is
qa.a: not case sensitive.

qa.q: The keyword that begins a comment in VHDL
qa.a: -- (two hyphens).

qa.q: A signal vs a variable in VHDL
qa.a: A signal represents a wire and updates after the process suspends; a variable updates immediately and exists only in the process.

qa.q: std_logic_vector(7 downto 0) represents
qa.a: an 8-bit bus with bit 7 as the MSB.

qa.q: Which statement is used for a multi-way branch inside a process?
qa.a: case ... when ... end case.

4.6.keyPoints: VHDL design flow: specification → HDL coding → simulation → synthesis → place & route → implementation (FPGA/ASIC).

5.1.title: Introduction to Computer Networks and Physical Layer

qa.q: Which layer provides end-to-end delivery and reliability?
qa.a: The transport layer.

qa.q: Which transmission mode is used by a walkie-talkie?
qa.a: Half duplex (both directions, but one at a time).

qa.q: Nyquist bit rate for a noiseless channel
qa.a: 2B log₂L, where L is the number of signal levels.

qa.q: Which device is used to connect networks with different protocols?
qa.a: Gateway.

qa.q: Which topology has the highest fault tolerance?
qa.a: Mesh.

5.1.keyPoints: TCP/IP layers: Application, Transport, Internet, Network Access (Link). Devices: repeater/hub (L1), bridge/switch (L2), router (L3), gateway (all layers).

5.2.title: Data Link Layer

qa.q: Which is the MAC broadcast address?
qa.a: FF:FF:FF:FF:FF:FF.

qa.q: Number of redundant bits in Hamming code for 4 data bits
The sublayers of the data link layer
qa.a: LLC (Logical Link Control) and MAC (Medium Access Control).

qa.q: Channel efficiency of stop-and-wait
qa.a: 1/(1 + 2a), where a = propagation time/transmission time.

qa.q: Maximum Ethernet (802.3) payload
qa.a: 1500 bytes (MTU).

5.2.keyPoints: Error control protocols: Stop-and-Wait ARQ (W = 1), Go-Back-N (Ws ≤ 2^m − 1, Wr = 1), Selective Repeat (Ws = Wr ≤ 2^(m−1)).

qa.q: Loopback address of IPv4
Which protocol assigns IP addresses automatically?
qa.a: DHCP (UDP ports 67/68).

qa.q: NAT is used to
qa.a: translate private IP addresses to a public IP address for Internet access.

qa.q: Number of subnets using /28 in a class C network
qa.a: 16 subnets (4 borrowed bits), each with 14 usable hosts.

qa.q: IPv4 header minimum size
qa.a: 20 bytes. IPv6 fixed header size: 40 bytes.

5.4.title: Transport Layer

qa.q: Which fields are in the TCP header but not UDP?
qa.a: Sequence number, acknowledgement number, window size, flags (SYN, ACK, FIN, RST, PSH, URG).

qa.q: What is the purpose of the PSH flag?
qa.a: Asks the receiver to deliver data to the application immediately.

qa.q: Port number used by DNS
Port used by Telnet
TCP congestion control phases
qa.a: slow start, congestion avoidance (AIMD), fast retransmit and fast recovery.

5.4.keyPoints: Common ports: FTP 20/21, SSH 22, Telnet 23, SMTP 25, DNS 53, DHCP 67/68, HTTP 80, POP3 110, IMAP 143, SNMP 161, HTTPS 443.

5.5.title: Application Layer

qa.q: Which DNS record gives an alias for a domain?
qa.a: CNAME.

qa.q: Which HTTP method is used to send form data to a server?
qa.a: POST (GET sends data in the URL).

qa.q: HTTP status code 404 means
qa.a: Not Found. 200 = OK, 301 = moved permanently, 500 = internal server error.

qa.q: Which protocol provides secure remote login?
qa.a: SSH.

qa.q: MIME is used for
qa.a: sending non-text data (images, attachments) through e-mail.

5.5.keyPoints: Application-layer paradigms: client-server (web, e-mail) vs peer-to-peer (BitTorrent). DNS resolution: recursive vs iterative queries.

5.6.title: Network Security

qa.q: Which algorithm is used for key exchange over an insecure channel?
qa.a: Diffie-Hellman.

qa.q: MD5 and SHA are
qa.a: hash functions producing a fixed-size message digest (MD5 = 128 bits, SHA-1 = 160 bits, SHA-256 = 256 bits).

qa.q: A DDoS attack is
qa.a: a distributed denial of service using many compromised machines (a botnet).

qa.q: A certificate authority (CA)
qa.a: issues digital certificates that bind public keys to identities (PKI).

qa.q: The port-based network access control standard is
qa.a: IEEE 802.1X.

5.6.keyPoints: Symmetric: DES, 3DES, AES, RC4 (fast, key sharing problem). Asymmetric: RSA, ECC, Diffie-Hellman (slow, solves key distribution).

6.1.title: Finite Automata and Regular Languages

qa.q: The number of states in the minimal DFA for strings over {a, b} ending with "ab"
A regular expression for strings with at least one a over {a, b}
Regular expression for all strings of even length over {a, b}
Which is more powerful: DFA, NFA or ε-NFA?
qa.a: All are equally powerful; they accept exactly the regular languages.

qa.q: Two-way finite automata recognize
qa.a: exactly the regular languages (no extra power).

6.1.keyPoints: RE identities: ε·R = R, ∅ + R = R, (R*)* = R*, R + R = R, ∅* = ε.

6.2.title: Context-Free Languages and Pushdown Automata

qa.q: The language of balanced parentheses is
qa.a: context-free but not regular.

qa.q: A grammar in which a variable derives itself as the leftmost symbol (A → Aα) has
qa.a: left recursion, which must be removed for top-down parsing.

qa.q: A PDA can accept by
qa.a: final state or by empty stack (equivalent in power for NPDAs).

qa.q: The language of palindromes over {a, b} is
qa.a: context-free but not deterministic context-free.

qa.q: Removing ε-productions, unit productions and useless symbols is done
qa.a: before converting a grammar to CNF.

6.2.keyPoints: CFLs are closed under union, concatenation, Kleene star, reversal, homomorphism and intersection with a regular language.

6.3.title: Turing Machines and Computability

qa.q: What is a decidable problem?
qa.a: A problem for which a TM always halts with the correct yes/no answer.

qa.q: Is P = NP?
qa.a: Unknown. It is the most famous open problem in computer science.

qa.q: NP-hard means
qa.a: every NP problem reduces to it in polynomial time; it need not be in NP itself.

qa.q: The complement of an RE but non-recursive language is
qa.a: not RE.

qa.q: Post Correspondence Problem is
qa.a: undecidable.

6.3.keyPoints: Relationships: Regular ⊂ CFL ⊂ CSL ⊂ Recursive ⊂ RE. P ⊆ NP; NP-complete = NP ∩ NP-hard.

6.4.title: Introduction to Computer Graphics and Graphics Hardware

qa.q: Refresh rate unit
qa.a: Hertz (frames per second).

qa.q: Aspect ratio of a display
qa.a: ratio of width to height, e.g. 16:9.

qa.q: Midpoint circle algorithm uses
qa.a: 8-way symmetry of the circle and an integer decision parameter.

qa.q: A color look-up table (palette)
qa.a: stores a limited set of colors; the frame buffer holds indices into it, saving memory.

qa.q: Bit planes: a frame buffer with 8 bits per pixel has
qa.a: 8 bit planes.

6.4.keyPoints: Bresenham decision parameter for |m| < 1: p₀ = 2Δy − Δx; if p < 0, next p = p + 2Δy, else p = p + 2Δy − 2Δx (and y increments).

6.5.title: Two-Dimensional Transformations, Viewing and Clipping

qa.q: The 2D rotation matrix about the origin in homogeneous form
qa.a: [[cos θ, −sin θ, 0], [sin θ, cos θ, 0], [0, 0, 1]].

qa.q: Reflection about the origin
qa.a: (x, y) → (−x, −y), equivalent to a 180° rotation.

qa.q: Scaling about a fixed point (xf, yf)
qa.a: translate to origin, scale, translate back.

qa.q: Which transformation preserves shape and size?
qa.a: Rigid-body transformations (translation, rotation, reflection).

qa.q: Inverse of a translation by (tx, ty)
qa.a: translation by (−tx, −ty).

6.5.keyPoints: Window-to-viewport mapping: xv = xvmin + (xw − xwmin)·sx, sx = (xvmax − xvmin)/(xwmax − xwmin); similarly for y.

6.6.title: Three-Dimensional Transformations and Projections

qa.q: Visible surface detection algorithm using a depth buffer
qa.a: Z-buffer (depth buffer) algorithm.

qa.q: The back-face detection test
qa.a: a polygon is a back face if its normal N and view direction V satisfy V·N > 0.

qa.q: Which projection is used in architectural drawings for realism?
qa.a: Perspective projection.

qa.q: Parallel projections are classified into
qa.a: orthographic and oblique.

qa.q: Number of vanishing points in a two-point perspective

6.6.keyPoints: Illumination: ambient + diffuse (Lambert, ∝ cos θ) + specular (Phong, ∝ cosⁿ α). Shading: flat, Gouraud (interpolate intensity), Phong (interpolate normals).

7.1.title: Data Structures: Lists, Stacks, Queues and Trees

qa.q: Infix to postfix conversion uses which data structure?
qa.a: Stack.

qa.q: The number of edges in a tree with n nodes
A complete binary tree with n nodes has height
qa.a: ⌊log₂ n⌋.

qa.q: Which traversal is used to delete a tree?
qa.a: Post-order (children before parent).

qa.q: Prefix form of (A + B) * C
qa.a: *+ABC.

7.1.keyPoints: Linked list vs array: array O(1) access, costly insert/delete; linked list O(n) access, O(1) insert/delete at a known position.

7.2.title: Sorting, Searching, Hashing and Graphs

qa.q: Worst-case complexity of heap sort
qa.a: O(n log n).

qa.q: Number of swaps in selection sort
qa.a: at most n − 1, which is its advantage.

qa.q: Time complexity of Dijkstra with a binary heap
qa.a: O((V + E) log V).

qa.q: Load factor of a hash table
qa.a: α = n/m (number of keys/table size).

qa.q: Which algorithm finds the MST by growing a tree from a vertex?
qa.a: Prim's algorithm.

7.2.keyPoints: Sorting complexities (avg): bubble/insertion/selection O(n²); merge/heap/quick O(n log n); radix O(d(n + k)). Binary search O(log n).

7.3.title: Data Models, Normalization and SQL

qa.q: Which SQL command removes a table completely?
qa.a: DROP TABLE. DELETE removes rows; TRUNCATE removes all rows quickly.

qa.q: Cardinality ratios in E-R model
A derived attribute is shown in an E-R diagram by
qa.a: a dashed ellipse (e.g. age derived from date of birth).

qa.q: Armstrong's axioms
qa.a: reflexivity, augmentation and transitivity.

qa.q: Natural join ⋈
qa.a: joins tuples with equal values on common attributes and keeps one copy of those attributes.

7.3.keyPoints: E-R symbols: rectangle = entity, double rectangle = weak entity, diamond = relationship, ellipse = attribute, double ellipse = multivalued, underline = key.

7.4.title: Transaction Processing, Concurrency Control and Recovery

qa.q: Serializability types
qa.a: conflict serializability and view serializability.

qa.q: Which lock allows a transaction to read and write?
qa.a: Exclusive (X) lock.

qa.q: Two-phase commit protocol is used in
qa.a: distributed databases to ensure all sites commit or all abort.

qa.q: A cascading rollback is
qa.a: when one transaction's failure forces rollback of others that read its uncommitted data.

qa.q: Shadow paging is
qa.a: a recovery technique that keeps a shadow page table unchanged and switches to the new table on commit.

7.4.keyPoints: Anomalies: lost update, dirty read, unrepeatable read, phantom read. SQL isolation levels: read uncommitted, read committed, repeatable read, serializable.

7.5.title: Operating System and Process Management

qa.q: Convoy effect occurs in
qa.a: FCFS scheduling (short jobs wait behind a long one).

qa.q: Turnaround time
qa.a: completion time − arrival time. Waiting time = turnaround time − burst time.

qa.q: The fork() system call
qa.a: creates a new child process.

qa.q: Resource allocation graph with a cycle and single-instance resources
qa.a: implies deadlock.

qa.q: Peterson's solution is for
qa.a: mutual exclusion between two processes.

7.5.keyPoints: Deadlock handling: prevention (break a condition), avoidance (Banker's), detection & recovery, or ignore (ostrich approach).

7.6.title: Memory Management, File Systems and System Administration

qa.q: Segmentation suffers from
qa.a: external fragmentation.

qa.q: Effective access time with TLB
qa.a: EAT = h(t_tlb + t_mem) + (1 − h)(t_tlb + 2 t_mem).

qa.q: Number of pages for a 32-bit address space with 4 KB pages
qa.a: 2²⁰ (about 1 million).

qa.q: Which disk scheduling algorithm is also called the elevator algorithm?
qa.a: SCAN.

qa.q: The FAT file system uses
qa.a: linked allocation with the links stored in a table (File Allocation Table).

7.6.keyPoints: Page replacement: FIFO, Optimal, LRU, LFU, Clock (second chance). Only FIFO suffers Belady's anomaly (stack algorithms like LRU and OPT do not).

8.1.title: Software Process and Requirements

qa.q: The waterfall model is suitable when
qa.a: requirements are well understood and stable.

qa.q: Feasibility study checks
qa.a: technical, economic, legal, operational and schedule feasibility.

qa.q: The RAD model emphasizes
qa.a: very short development cycles using component reuse and CASE tools.

qa.q: Which model combines waterfall with iterations and risk analysis?
qa.a: The spiral model.

qa.q: Requirement engineering process steps
qa.a: feasibility study, elicitation & analysis, specification, validation, management.

8.1.keyPoints: Software quality attributes (McCall/ISO 25010): correctness, reliability, efficiency, integrity/security, usability, maintainability, testability, portability, reusability, interoperability.

8.2.title: Software Design and Architecture

qa.q: Fan-in and fan-out
qa.a: fan-in = number of modules that call a module (high is good); fan-out = number of modules it calls (keep moderate).

qa.q: The MVC pattern separates
qa.a: Model (data), View (presentation) and Controller (input handling).

qa.q: Layered architecture example
qa.a: OSI model; each layer serves the one above it.

qa.q: Coupling where modules share global data is
qa.a: common coupling.

qa.q: Stamp coupling
qa.a: passing a whole data structure when only part of it is needed.

8.2.keyPoints: Design concepts: abstraction, refinement, modularity, architecture, information hiding, functional independence (cohesion/coupling), refactoring.

8.3.title: Software Testing, Cost Estimation, Quality and Configuration Management

qa.q: Equivalence partitioning
qa.a: divides input data into classes that should be treated the same, testing one value from each.

qa.q: Verification vs validation
qa.a: verification: "Are we building the product right?"; validation: "Are we building the right product?"

qa.q: Smoke testing
qa.a: a quick test of the main functions to decide whether a build is stable enough for further testing.

qa.q: Putnam model is based on
qa.a: the Rayleigh curve for staffing over project duration.

qa.q: Software configuration items (SCIs)
qa.a: work products under configuration control: SRS, design, code, test plans, manuals.

8.3.keyPoints: Testing levels: unit → integration → system → acceptance. White-box: statement, branch, path coverage. Black-box: equivalence partitioning, BVA, cause-effect graphing.

8.4.title: Object-Oriented Fundamentals and Analysis

qa.q: Number of diagrams in UML 2.x
qa.a: 14 (7 structural, 7 behavioral).

qa.q: Which diagram shows physical nodes and deployed artifacts?
qa.a: Deployment diagram.

qa.q: Association class
qa.a: a class attached to an association that holds attributes of the relationship itself.

qa.q: A use case describes
qa.a: a sequence of actions a system performs that yields an observable result of value to an actor.

qa.q: Which UP phase establishes the architecture baseline?
qa.a: Elaboration.

8.4.keyPoints: UML structural diagrams: class, object, component, deployment, package, composite structure, profile. Behavioral: use case, activity, state machine, sequence, communication, timing, interaction overview.

8.5.title: Object-Oriented Design

qa.q: GRASP stands for
qa.a: General Responsibility Assignment Software Patterns.

qa.q: The 9 GRASP patterns
qa.a: Information Expert, Creator, Controller, Low Coupling, High Cohesion, Polymorphism, Pure Fabrication, Indirection, Protected Variations.

qa.q: Pure Fabrication
qa.a: an invented class (not a domain concept) to achieve high cohesion and low coupling (e.g. a PersistentStorage class).

qa.q: Facade pattern
qa.a: provides a single simplified interface to a complex subsystem.

qa.q: Strategy pattern
qa.a: encapsulates interchangeable algorithms behind a common interface.

8.5.keyPoints: Creational: Singleton, Factory Method, Abstract Factory, Builder, Prototype. Structural: Adapter, Bridge, Composite, Decorator, Facade, Flyweight, Proxy. Behavioral: Observer, Strategy, Command, Iterator, State, Template Method, etc.

8.6.title: Object-Oriented Design Implementation

qa.q: Unit tests should be
qa.a: automated, independent and repeatable.

qa.q: Which UML element maps to an abstract class or interface in code?
qa.a: A class marked {abstract}/italic, or an «interface».

qa.q: Code smells
qa.a: symptoms (duplicate code, long methods, large classes) indicating a need for refactoring.

qa.q: Continuous integration
qa.a: frequently merging code to a shared repository with automated builds and tests.

qa.q: Mapping an association with multiplicity 0..1 in code
qa.a: a reference attribute that may be null.

8.6.keyPoints: Implementation flow in OOAD (Larman): DCD → class definitions; interaction diagrams → method bodies; implement from least to most coupled; write tests first.

9.1.title: Introduction to AI and Intelligent Agents

qa.q: Rationality of an agent depends on
qa.a: the performance measure, prior knowledge, available actions and percept sequence to date.

qa.q: An episodic environment is one where
qa.a: each episode (percept-action) is independent of previous ones, e.g. image classification.

qa.q: Weak AI vs strong AI
qa.a: Weak AI: machines act intelligently (narrow tasks). Strong AI: machines genuinely think and have minds.

qa.q: ELIZA was
qa.a: an early (1966) natural language program simulating a psychotherapist.

qa.q: An example of a multi-agent environment
qa.a: chess, football, taxi driving.

9.1.keyPoints: Agent types (simple → complex): simple reflex, model-based reflex, goal-based, utility-based, learning agent.

9.2.title: Problem Solving and Searching Techniques

qa.q: Which search is optimal with non-negative step costs and no heuristic?
qa.a: Uniform cost search.

qa.q: A consistent (monotonic) heuristic satisfies
qa.a: h(n) ≤ c(n, a, n') + h(n') for every successor n'.

qa.q: Backtracking search for CSPs is improved by
qa.a: MRV (minimum remaining values), degree heuristic, least constraining value, and forward checking/arc consistency.

qa.q: Local beam search
qa.a: keeps k states instead of one and selects the k best successors.

qa.q: Tic-tac-toe game tree is searched using
qa.a: minimax (with alpha-beta pruning).

9.2.keyPoints: Search comparison: BFS O(b^d) time/space; DFS O(b^m) time, O(bm) space; IDS O(b^d) time, O(bd) space; A* optimal with admissible h.

9.3.title: Knowledge Representation and Reasoning

qa.q: Horn clause
qa.a: a clause with at most one positive literal; used in Prolog and forward/backward chaining.

qa.q: Universal instantiation
qa.a: infers P(a) from ∀x P(x) for any constant a.

qa.q: Conditional independence in Bayesian networks
qa.a: a node is independent of its non-descendants given its parents.

qa.q: Scripts in knowledge representation
qa.a: represent stereotyped sequences of events (e.g. a restaurant visit).

qa.q: Which logic handles degrees of truth?
qa.a: Fuzzy logic.

9.3.keyPoints: Equivalences: P → Q ≡ ¬Q → ¬P (contrapositive); ¬(P ∧ Q) ≡ ¬P ∨ ¬Q; ¬(P ∨ Q) ≡ ¬P ∧ ¬Q; ¬∀x P ≡ ∃x ¬P.

9.4.title: Expert Systems, NLP, Machine Vision and Robotics

qa.q: Who is responsible for building the knowledge base?
qa.a: The knowledge engineer, working with the domain expert.

qa.q: DENDRAL was
qa.a: an early expert system for identifying chemical structures from mass-spectrometry data.

qa.q: Part-of-speech tagging
qa.a: assigns word classes (noun, verb, adjective) to each token.

qa.q: Named Entity Recognition
qa.a: identifies names of people, places, organizations, dates in text.

qa.q: Degrees of freedom of a robot
qa.a: the number of independent movements (joints) it can make; a typical industrial arm has 6.

9.4.keyPoints: NLP stages: morphological → lexical → syntactic → semantic → discourse integration → pragmatic analysis.

9.5.title: Machine Learning, Fuzzy Logic and Genetic Algorithms

qa.q: Gini index is used in
qa.a: CART decision trees as an impurity measure.

qa.q: Unsupervised learning examples
qa.a: clustering (k-means, hierarchical) and association rule mining (Apriori).

qa.q: Crossover types in GA
qa.a: single-point, two-point, uniform.

qa.q: Elitism in GA
qa.a: copies the best individuals unchanged to the next generation.

qa.q: Exploration vs exploitation
qa.a: In RL, trying new actions (exploration) vs using known best actions (exploitation), e.g. ε-greedy.

9.5.keyPoints: Fuzzy membership functions: triangular, trapezoidal, Gaussian. Inference: Mamdani (fuzzy output + defuzzification) vs Sugeno (crisp functional output).

9.6.title: Neural Networks

qa.q: Number of layers in a perceptron that can solve XOR
qa.a: at least 2 layers of weights (input → hidden → output).

qa.q: Softmax activation is used for
qa.a: multi-class classification outputs (probabilities summing to 1).

qa.q: Momentum in gradient descent
qa.a: adds a fraction of the previous update to speed convergence and reduce oscillation.

qa.q: CNNs are mainly used for
qa.a: image data; RNNs/LSTMs for sequential data.

qa.q: Adaline differs from perceptron
qa.a: it updates weights using the linear (pre-activation) output with the LMS/delta rule.

9.6.keyPoints: Learning paradigms in ANN: supervised (backprop, perceptron), unsupervised (Hebbian, Kohonen SOM), reinforcement. Loss minimized by gradient descent: w ← w − η∂E/∂w.

10.1.title: Engineering Drawing and its Concepts

qa.q: Which projection is recommended by the Bureau of Indian Standards and commonly used in Nepal?
qa.a: First-angle projection.

qa.q: Dimension lines are drawn as
qa.a: thin continuous lines with arrowheads.

qa.q: A sectional view is drawn to
qa.a: show the interior details of an object.

qa.q: The standard A4 sheet size is
Cutting plane lines are shown as
qa.a: thin chain lines, thick at the ends and at changes of direction.

10.1.keyPoints: Line types: continuous thick (visible outlines), continuous thin (dimension, hatching), dashed (hidden), chain thin (centre lines), chain thick at ends (cutting plane).

10.2.title: Engineering Economics

qa.q: Present worth of an annuity
Future worth of an annuity
Sinking fund factor (A/F)
Sum-of-years' digits depreciation for year k
qa.a: (n − k + 1)/[n(n + 1)/2] × (cost − salvage).

qa.q: Discounted payback period
qa.a: the time to recover the investment using discounted cash flows.

10.2.keyPoints: Rule of 72: money doubles in about 72/i years at i% compound interest. Accept projects with NPV > 0, IRR > MARR, B/C > 1.

10.3.title: Project Planning and Scheduling

qa.q: Standard deviation of the project duration in PERT
qa.a: √(sum of variances of critical activities).

qa.q: Probability of completing a project by time T in PERT
qa.a: uses Z = (T − Te)/σ and the normal distribution table.

qa.q: Independent float
qa.a: EST(j) − LFT(i) − duration; may be negative (then taken as zero).

qa.q: Activity-on-node (AON) networks
qa.a: represent activities as nodes; no dummy activities are needed.

qa.q: A project with 3 parallel paths of 10, 12 and 15 days duration takes
qa.a: 15 days (the longest path is critical).

10.3.keyPoints: Network rules: EST(start) = 0; EFT = EST + duration; LFT(end) = project duration; LST = LFT − duration; critical activities have EST = LST.

10.4.title: Project Management

qa.q: Schedule Variance
qa.a: SV = EV − PV (negative means behind schedule).

qa.q: Cost Variance
qa.a: CV = EV − AC (negative means over budget).

qa.q: Estimate at completion (typical)
qa.a: EAC = BAC/CPI.

qa.q: Project charter
qa.a: the document that formally authorizes the project and the project manager.

qa.q: Types of tender
qa.a: open, limited (restricted), and negotiated/direct procurement.

10.4.keyPoints: EVM: PV (planned), EV (earned), AC (actual), BAC (budget at completion); CPI = EV/AC, SPI = EV/PV.

10.5.title: Engineering Professional Practice and Ethics

qa.q: An engineer's duty to the employer includes
qa.a: faithful service, loyalty, confidentiality, and avoiding conflicts of interest.

qa.q: Professional liability insurance
qa.a: covers claims arising from errors or negligence in professional services.

qa.q: A patent protects
qa.a: new, useful and non-obvious inventions for a limited period.

qa.q: Trademark protects
qa.a: distinctive names, logos and symbols identifying goods or services.

qa.q: Cyber crime under Nepal's Electronic Transactions Act includes
qa.a: unauthorized access, damage to computer systems, and publishing illegal material electronically.

10.5.keyPoints: Ethical dilemmas are resolved by prioritizing: public safety → law → client/employer → profession → self.

10.6.title: Engineering Regulatory Body (Nepal Engineering Council)

qa.q: Where is the Nepal Engineering Council office located?
qa.a: Minbhawan, Kathmandu.

qa.q: How many members (councilors) are in the Council?
qa.a: 21 councilors.

qa.q: Who appoints the NEC chairperson?
qa.a: The Government of Nepal (an engineer with at least 15 years' post-bachelor experience).

qa.q: Is NEC registration automatic after graduation?
qa.a: No. Since the 2079 amendment, passing the registration exam is mandatory.

qa.q: NEC registration exam is conducted how many times a year?
qa.a: Four times a year, per the annual calendar.

10.6.keyPoints: NEC Act 2055 (amended 2079) + NEC Regulations 2057 (amended 2080) govern registration, code of conduct and the licensing exam.
